items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: all of a sudden you become a Stan Kenton

ctx.x: Yes. Hot jazz, as opposed to cool jazz. I think it’s just a physical thing. I mean certain people like to live in Spain, certain people like to live in Vermont. I mean people make a lot of this. There is room for all of them. I happen to have been weaned, early on, not only on Louis Armstrong and Bix Beiderbecke and Bessie Smith and Duke Ellington, of course. When I was just thirteen and fourteen it was wonderful in New York particularly because we had disc jockeys, jazz disc jockeys, who didn’t, who were very…

You know they’re forty years old and they’re passé. Ridiculous. Ridiculous. What do they want from a guy? That he change his colors every five years which way the wind blows, all of a sudden you become a Stan Kenton, you change from— So anyway—
Was it mostly the non-musicians that started that? Was it the writers and the critics?
